title: Multiply and divide integers using the sign rules

lesson.title: Sign Rules for Times and Divide

steps.say: You already know how to subtract integers, like nine minus negative four. Today we add one small tool: what happens to the sign when we multiply or divide two integers. It is really just two little rules.

Start with what multiplying means: equal groups. Imagine you borrow four dollars from a friend for a bubble tea, three weeks in a row. That is three groups of negative four dollars. Three groups of four is twelve, and every group is money you owe, so the answer is negative twelve.

Division is the same picture read backwards. You owe twelve dollars in total, spread evenly over three weeks. Twelve shared into three groups is four per group, and it is still money owed, so negative twelve divided by three is negative four. Notice both times: one negative and one positive gave a negative answer.

visual.caption: $12 owed, split into 3 equal weeks → $4 owed each week

steps.say: Now the other rule: when both numbers are negative, the answer turns positive. Think of it as taking debt away. If your parents cancel five of your two dollar debts, you are ten dollars better off. So negative five times negative two is positive ten. Here is the whole idea in one line: same signs give a positive, different signs give a negative.

Careful — here is the trap almost everyone falls into. These sign rules are only for times and divide. Someone sees negative three plus negative four, spots two negatives, and writes seven. But adding is not grouping, it is stacking. Owing three dollars and then owing four more means you owe seven, so the answer is negative seven. Two negatives only make a positive when you multiply or divide.

visual.caption: Start at −3, owe $4 more, land on −7 (not +7)

steps.say: So here is your takeaway: for times and divide, same signs make a positive and different signs make a negative — and for plus and minus, keep thinking about the number line instead.

lesson.answer: When you multiply or divide: same signs → positive, different signs → negative. Adding does not follow this rule.

practice.question: Your water bottle has a slow leak and loses 5 millilitres every minute, so each minute counts as negative five. First work out negative five times six. Then work out negative thirty divided by negative five. You can draw six groups of negative five if that helps.
practice.answer: Negative five times six is negative thirty (different signs → negative), so the bottle loses 30 millilitres in six minutes. Negative thirty divided by negative five is positive six (same signs → positive), which tells you it took 6 minutes.
